prize_parts.citation: For a visionary, densely patterned prose, rooted in his poetry, that builds memory, the body and dream into a singular metaphysical architecture.

statement.case_for: My choice of writer is unchanged, but my citation is narrower than in round 1, and I replaced B033 with B003 as an alternative after the exchange. The case for Cărtărescu rests on the criteria alone. The voice is recognizable within a page: long, rhythmically built sentences with a hallucinatory, encyclopedic imagination. The formal achievement is that the Blinding (Orbitor) trilogy and Solenoid appear, on public knowledge, to be built as large structures rather than piled-up episodes. The imaginative and intellectual depth lies in one sustained metaphysical project anchored in the body, memory and Bucharest. The oeuvre spans decades and several genres. The citation I now propose puts the large-scale prose at the center and names the poetry only as its root, as Mattson suggested, because I would otherwise claim more than the evidence supports. Mattson and Sward also say the case should not lean on post-communist context. I agree, and that context should carry no weight in the citation. The chair asked whether I would accept a prose-only citation if the poetry cannot be assessed. I would, since the case for prose does not depend on the poetry. The agreement among Mattson, Sward and me is not evidence of merit. It only means that three readers with the same limits of evidence reached similar judgments.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains the length and recurrence of the late novels. Olsson, Sward and Mattson have each named it, and I cannot settle it from the supplied record. I distinguished recurrent motif from recurrent method in round 1, but that distinction is an argument and not evidence. The case holds only if the later books change the terms of the project in construction, scale or the relation between the voice and its material. If a reader of the Romanian finds mainly rework of earlier imagery, the claim of sustained development weakens considerably. The second reservation is translation. His effects depend on syntactic density and rhythm that I can judge only through translation. Coverage of the poetry and early work is uneven, so any citation scope beyond the major prose is less well supported. Carson and Can Xue have real advantages that Cărtărescu lacks: Carson has line-level economy, and Can Xue has a method that is radical and compressed.

responses.point: Olsson ranks Can Xue first for a sustained, anti-realist method that dissolves psychology, space and causality. He weighs the length and recurrence of Cărtărescu's novels as a cost to formal economy. He asks what evidence would move members on B003, and says a regional expert report is the right way to test whether her strangeness survives at sentence level.
responses.response: I accept the procedural point and I would support an expert report on her Chinese prose before a final judgment. My low ranking of her reflects my own inability to judge her sentences, not a negative view of the work. Your economy argument is the most serious objection to my choice, and I cannot refute it from this record. We seem to disagree on what counts as repetition. You treat recurrence in Cărtărescu as a flaw of economy. I treat it as possibly structural, and equally ask whether consistency in her method is depth or limited range. Neither of us can answer that from translations alone. I have therefore moved B003 into my alternatives. The reason is not any count of supporters. I now think the question of development is as open for her as for him, and she offers a more compressed form.

responses.point: Carlberg ranks Carson first and answers my round-1 point by saying that compactness is not shallowness. A formally varied, coherent corpus can show sustained quality, and she reads the idealistic direction through the elegiac and ethical seriousness of Carson's treatment of love and loss. She would build the citation on poetry, essay and hybrid narrative, not on translation.
responses.response: That is a fair correction. I should not equate scale with depth, and a coherent compact oeuvre can be depth. The citation you describe, naming poetry, essay and hybrid narrative and leaving translation out as a ground, would answer the scope problem I raised, and I would regard it as defensible. My remaining difficulty is evidential. I cannot tell from public knowledge which volumes beyond Autobiography of Red and Nox carry the claim of a durable core. Your answer, that desire, loss and the classical text return across forms, is plausible but is not yet a demonstration. That is why Carson remains my first alternative. Her case could outweigh mine if a committee reader showed that the core survives across the whole bibliography.

responses.point: Mattson agrees on the formal claim for Cărtărescu but would put less weight on post-communist context. She wants the citation to stay with the prose, with poetry as the stated root, until the committee has more evidence on the poetry. She names Can Xue as a serious rival if development can be shown.
responses.response: I accept this and have changed my citation to match: prose at the center, poetry as root. My round-1 wording said 'prose and poetry', which claimed more than my evidence supports. I also withdraw the weight I placed on post-communist experience. It describes the setting, and the case should rest on how the books are built. Your remark about Can Xue as a rival to your first choice, with a test through the later work, seems right to me, and I would apply the same test to Cărtărescu's late cycle. We agree on both the claim and its limits, so I do not treat that as confirmation.

responses.point: Palm ranks Carson first. She accepts that Cărtărescu's architecture is a real achievement but says the length and recurring motifs of the late novels give her pause. She weighs line-level control and formal economy above scale, and doubts that the visual and material formats can be judged by text alone.
responses.response: I share your doubt about Nox. If its force is partly physical, it should not carry a citation, and I would rest a Carson case on Autobiography of Red and the lyric and essay work. Where we differ is the weighting. You put line-level economy first. I put sustained construction first, because the Nobel criterion of significance across a whole body of work seems to me harder to meet with a compact, varied corpus. I do not think translation separates us. We both judge through translation, and I still cannot prove to you that the late novels avoid recurrence. For that reason I would not call my weighting more than a judgment.

uncertainties: Translation: I cannot judge the effect of Cărtărescu's dense Romanian prose, and the same limit applies to Can Xue, Tawada, Zurita and the other non-English writers. Comparisons across candidates therefore rest on partial evidence.
Corpus coverage: the poetry, essays and early prose are unevenly covered in translation. This is why I have narrowed the citation to prose with poetry as root.
Whether the late long novels extend the project or recycle it is unresolved. It is the main risk to my choice, and I cannot answer it from public knowledge.
The weighting of sustained architectural scale against compact formal range, which now separates B045 from B004, is a matter of judgment and not of evidence.

Whether Can Xue's method develops, and whether the strangeness is built into her sentences, needs a reader of the Chinese or an anonymous regional expert report. My move of B003 into my alternatives is provisional.
I have not independently verified any source. All assessments rest on general public knowledge and the supplied entries, and the committee's expert reports are not part of this evidence.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. The profile documents long ties to the culture sections of Svenska Dagbladet and Dagens Nyheter, where I am a critic, and to Prague and Vienna literary milieus. It records no documented connection to any shortlisted writer. My own practice as a novelist of documentary historical fiction is context and not evidence of preference. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
